<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="טבת_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916270_theRebbe_968" batchId="meluket-_D7_98_D7_91_D7_AA_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916270_theRebbe_968__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the date and heading for the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbat Parshat Shemot,</t>
    <t s="2">23 Tevet*,</t>
    <t s="3">Rosh Chodesh Shvat,</t>
    <t s="4">the year 5713**</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the verse "She who dwells in the gardens...", interpreting it as referring to the revelation of the Garden of Eden and the future revelation, which is a leap from the immanent light to the encompassing light.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"She who dwells in the gardens, etc., my Beloved has fled, etc., upon the mountains of spices"1,</t>
    <t s="1">and the Admor</t>
    <t s="2">(the Horav Shalom Ber)</t>
    <t s="3">of blessed memory explains in his maamar beginning with these words2</t>
    <t s="4">which he said on 24 Tevet3</t>
    <t s="5">(the day of the yahrzeit of the Alter Rebbe),</t>
    <t s="6">that "she who dwells in the gardens" speaks of the revelation of the Garden of Eden4,</t>
    <t s="7">"gardens"</t>
    <t s="8">(in the plural)</t>
    <t s="9">are5</t>
    <t s="10">the lower Garden of Eden and the upper Garden of Eden, which are in Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah</t>
    <t s="11">(the lower Garden of Eden is in Asiyah, and the upper Garden of Eden is in Beriah6),</t>
    <t s="12">and "she who dwells in the gardens" means7</t>
    <t s="13">Malchut of Atzilut, which contracts itself to dwell in the gardens,</t>
    <t s="14">and "my Beloved has fled, etc., upon the mountains of spices" speaks of the revelation of the future,</t>
    <t s="15">which is vastly superior, even beyond comparison, to the revelation of the Garden of Eden,</t>
    <t s="16">for the revelation of the Garden of Eden is the immanent light, and the revelation of the future is the encompassing light.</t>
    <t s="17">For this is the meaning of "fled, etc., upon the mountains of spices"</t>
    <t s="18">(specifically "fled"),</t>
    <t s="19">that the ascent from the revelation of the Garden of Eden to the revelation of the future is by way of flight and leap, not in order and gradation.</t>
    <t s="20">Nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="21">in order to receive the revelation of the encompassing light of the future,</t>
    <t s="22">it is specifically through the prior revelation of the immanent light of the Garden of Eden.</t>
    <t s="23">And this is "she who dwells in the gardens"</t>
    <t s="24">(and afterwards)</t>
    <t s="25">"my Beloved has fled, etc., upon the mountains of spices",</t>
    <t s="26">that first there must be the revelation of "she who dwells in the gardens," and through this specifically one arrives</t>
    <t s="27">(by way of flight and leap)</t>
    <t s="28">at the revelation of "the mountains of spices."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the difference between immanent and encompassing light, arguing that the immanent light inherently has a relationship to division, as proven by the fact that the encompassing light is not affected by vessels.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation of the matter:</t>
    <t s="2">The difference between immanent light and encompassing light is,</t>
    <t s="3">that encompassing light is simple light,</t>
    <t s="4">while immanent light comes in division,</t>
    <t s="5">the light of wisdom, the light of kindness, etc.</t>
    <t s="6">And it is explained in the aforementioned maamar,</t>
    <t s="7">that from the fact that immanent light comes in division,</t>
    <t s="8">even though the actual division is caused by its being clothed in the vessels,</t>
    <t s="9">it is necessary to say,</t>
    <t s="10">that also in the light itself</t>
    <t s="11">(before its clothing in vessels)</t>
    <t s="12">there is a relationship to division.</t>
    <t s="13">For in the Pardes8</t>
    <t s="14">it is explained,</t>
    <t s="15">that the division that occurs in the light through its clothing in vessels,</t>
    <t s="16">is only with regard to its activity</t>
    <t s="17">(in what manner it acts upon the creations,</t>
    <t s="18">for when it is clothed in the vessel of kindness, it performs the activity of kindness,</t>
    <t s="19">and so on with all the Sefiros),</t>
    <t s="20">but the light itself remains in its simplicity.</t>
    <t s="21">And based on this, one could say,</t>
    <t s="22">that the light, in and of itself</t>
    <t s="23">(before its clothing in vessels)</t>
    <t s="24">is completely simple</t>
    <t s="25">(that it has no relationship to division at all),</t>
    <t s="26">like the analogy of sunlight</t>
    <t s="27">(brought in the Pardes8),</t>
    <t s="28">that although in itself it is simple light</t>
    <t s="29">(for light is of the same kind as the luminary and is attached to the luminary),</t>
    <t s="30">nevertheless, when it shines through a white, red, or green glass,</t>
    <t s="31">it appears</t>
    <t s="32">(and acts)</t>
    <t s="33">according to the color of the vessel.</t>
    <t s="34">However, at first glance, this explanation is insufficient9.</t>
    <t s="35">For it is known10,</t>
    <t s="36">that encompassing light,</t>
    <t s="37">even when it shines within the vessels,</t>
    <t s="38">the vessel does not effect a change in it,</t>
    <t s="39">not even that it should appear according to the manner of the vessel</t>
    <t s="40">[and as is also brought in the aforementioned maamar,</t>
    <t s="41">that the light of Atik11,</t>
    <t s="42">even as it is drawn into Zeir Anpin,</t>
    <t s="43">is in the category of simplicity].</t>
    <t s="44">And from this it is proven10,</t>
    <t s="45">that this, that in immanent light there occurs</t>
    <t s="46">(through the vessels)</t>
    <t s="47">a form and division</t>
    <t s="48">(with regard to its activity, at least)</t>
    <t s="49">is because this light</t>
    <t s="50">(even before its clothing in vessels)</t>
    <t s="51">is of the category of division.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
